_comment: Hand-maintained, like errata.json. Not overwritten by tools/extract.py. Encodes the *order* of the procedures the booklet describes in prose (r202-r205, r215-r217) so `bp start`, `bp day` and `bp move` can walk them step by step instead of an LLM reassembling them from the text each turn. Every entry cites the section it comes from; nothing here restates game content that data/sections.json already holds.

readings._comment: A few sections send the reader away and tell them to come back - e001 does it twice. Rather than read the whole section at once and lose the pauses the text itself asks for, `bp show <id>#<part>` prints one passage at a time. Anchors are quoted phrases from the body, matched whitespace-insensitively so the pdftotext line wrapping does not matter; if an anchor stops matching after a re-extraction, `bp` refuses rather than printing the wrong passage. No game text is copied here.

e001.what: The premise: the assassination, the 500 gold, the ten weeks.
e001.until: and then return to this event and read the paragraph below:
e001.then: The text itself stops here. Do r202 (wit & wiles) and the starting gold, then come back for e001#caravan.

e001.from: To escape the mercenary and royal guard
e001.then: Ask for 1d6, then bp start <die>. Reading the list of six destinations aloud is optional - the die picks one.

e001.what: Dawn on day 1, and the standing e002 warning.
e001.from: Now, at dawn you roll out of the merchant wagons

readings._comment2: e060, e068 and e105 are the other shape: a lettered tail paragraph (e060a, e068a, e105a) that only happens on some die results. It is written as prose rather than as a table row, so `options` used to print it as part of the setup and hand over an outcome the player had not rolled for. Splitting them makes the first part the pre-roll setup, which is all `options` shows.

e060.what: Arrested. Read this, then ask for 1d6 for the gravity of the offence.
e060.then: 1 or less-e061; 2-e062; 3,4-e063; 5,6-read e060#minor. e060 has no parsed table, so resolve it by reading this line, not with `bp resolve`.

e060.what: Minor Offence - the 5,6 outcome. Do not read before the die.

e068.what: Wizard's Abode. Read this, then ask for 1d6.
e068.then: bp resolve e068 <die>. On 5,6 that is e068#tower.

e068.what: Wizard Tower - the 5,6 outcome. Do not read before the die.

e105.what: Storm Clouds Ahead. Read this, then ask for 1d6 if they fly on.
e105.then: bp resolve e105 <die>. On 6 that is e105#weather.

e105.what: Violent Weather - the 6 outcome. Do not read before the die.

readings._comment3: e002's text opens with the die that decides whether the guardsmen appear at all. By the time the section is read out that roll has already been made, so the reading starts at the guardsmen themselves.

e002.what: The guardsmen themselves; the trigger die is rolled before this.

setup.goal: Collect 500 gold pieces and return to the Northlands within 10 weeks (70 days). Day 71 is a loss, and so is the Prince's death.

steps.prompt: Read the opening aloud. It ends by sending you to r202 - stop there.
Roll 1d6 for wit & wiles. A result of 1 counts as 2.
steps.note: Replaying: if they won last time they may take wit & wiles one lower, if they lost, one higher.

steps.prompt: Roll 1d6 for starting gold: wealth code 2 on the Treasure Table.
Read the caravan paragraph, then ask where the caravan dropped them.
Read the closing paragraph: dawn in the ditch, and the standing e002 warning.
Write the sheet down before play starts, so no number is carried in memory.
steps.note: From then on bp game reads it back, and bp time/food/gold/party/eat/lodge change it. Every follower who joins gets bp party add with the combat skill and endurance the section printed.

hexes.3: Ruins of Jakor's Keep (0901 - e001 prints 0801, which is a typo; see errata.json)

standing: e002 is checked at the end of any day finishing north of the Tragoth River, after events but before the evening meal (e001, r215).

All six starting hexes are north of the Tragoth. e001's 'southern border' is the southern border of the Northlands Kingdom, which is the NORTH edge of the map - the Prince fled south and has not got clear yet. So expect e002 at the end of day 1 and every day until the party crosses the river southward. Getting south of the Tragoth is what the early game is about.
Ogon (0101) and Weshor (1501) add +1 to the e002 roll, and both are starting hexes - the guard looks hardest for you in the towns you might have run to.

actions.name: rest
actions.note: Heals one wound per character if no combat or escape happens. Still check for a travel event as if entering your own hex (r222), and rest improves hunting (r215).

actions.name: search cache
actions.note: Only for a cache you previously placed.

endofday.what: If the day ends north of the Tragoth River, check e002 now - after events, before the meal.
Feed the whole party. Mounts need fodder in terrain where the travel table says fodder is no.
Anyone who cannot be fed starves - resolve r216.
Pay the day's wages to any hired follower at the meal - unpaid hirelings leave.
In a town, castle or temple, lodging must usually be bought.
Advance the time track one day. The game is lost on day 71.

day.one_action_note: One action per day, and the whole party does it. Some events grant a bonus action, others force the time track forward several days (r203).

move.lost_terrain_conflict: r205 says the lost check uses the terrain you are LEAVING; r205d says the post-river check uses the terrain of the new hex you are ENTERING. Both are quoted as printed - the specific rule is used for the river step and the general rule elsewhere. Travel events always use the terrain ENTERED (r204b).

speeds.foot: 1 hex per day if anyone is unmounted (r204a).
speeds.mounted: 1 or 2 hexes per day if everyone is mounted (r204a).
speeds.airborne: up to 3 hexes per day on winged mounts, flying all day, landing to camp (r204a). Winged parties may instead short-hop 1-2 hexes as normal mounted travel.

move.after_event: A travel event normally consumes the rest of the day (r204f). Exceptions: a fight where you killed everyone, and encounters that were only talk or negotiation - travel may continue if speed remains.
